description: Versioned runtime configuration and skill digests for the reproducible Craft sandbox image (docker/craft/Dockerfile). The image bakes this file at /etc/craft/runtime-config.json; the service-side executor verifies it before accepting a sandbox for delegation.

opencode.digest_provenance: linux-amd64/linux-arm64 were hashed from the official v1.18.4 release tarballs (opencode-linux-x64.tar.gz, opencode-linux-arm64.tar.gz) on 2026-09-14 and pinned here plus in the Dockerfile build args; darwin-arm64 is the R01 local probe carried in opencode.lock.json.
opencode.health_check: opencode --version must print exactly 1.18.4 AND the installed binary's sha256 must equal the pinned per-arch digest before a sandbox is accepted; GET /doc info.version=1.0.0 is a static OpenAPI constant and must never be used as the version signal.

skill_digest_rule: Every skill mounted into the runtime must appear here with the SHA-256 of its installed bundle; the executor refuses skills whose digest is not listed. Entries are appended by the skill packaging chain; this file is versioned with the image.

limits.scope: internal-trial quotas only; no paid execution is enabled by this configuration before gate G4 passes.

permissions.rule: No tool ever receives a broad always-allow. Anything not explicitly listed resolves to ask (R06 owns the ask interaction flow); webfetch stays denied until the sandbox egress policy explicitly lists an allowed destination set. Read-only discovery of the staged material is the only allow tier.

workspace.inputs_contract: Root-owned 0555 and mounted read-only at run time; staged only by the platform's authorized workspace writer (inputs/<sha256>/<name>), never written by the OpenCode process.
workspace.output_contract: Owned by the craft runtime user (UID/GID 10001) and writable; artifact versions are published from here by the service, not by the model directly.

credentials.rule: No account keys, platform long-lived tokens or user credentials are baked into, or mounted under, this image or the workspace. Model access flows exclusively through the server-provided gateway or an authorized BYOK entry managed by the platform; the OpenCode process never holds tenant or platform credentials.
